title: Race calculator
type.hike_tip: Hiking: day hikes, mid-elevation mountains and Taiwan's 100 Peaks (Baiyue) alike, one day or several.
trip.label: Trip
trip.hint: Required: rests and pacing differ a lot between the two
trip.tip: Guided group: the main number is the group time — your capacity time × your group factor when the back-test found that more accurate (altitude and pack taken out), else the time your past group days' EP/h give — with your capacity time beside it; on your own: the main number is your capacity time (your walking capacity at AeT: the steep walking windows of your trail runs plus the climbing windows of your hikes at HR ≥ AeT).
calc.tip: A red * is required. Once everything is filled in, every change recalculates on its own; Calculate recalculates right away. With a season-plan event selected, the inputs and result are saved with that event and come back the next time you pick it.
adv.title: Advanced options
adv.hint: Segments, pacing, heat: the defaults are fine; open to adjust
chart.title: Segment targets
chart.tip:
Each segment's target pace, power or heart rate along the course.
How to read: distance (km) across, one measure up; the light area is the elevation profile; hover the chart or click the table for a segment's details.
Look for: flats and runnable climbs (3–8 %) by power; steep (> 8 %) or walked climbs by an HR cap; trail descents by neither, so they are blank on the power / HR chart; on races > 3 h the HR cap is AeT. On trail the HR cap is one number for the whole race; late in the race HR drops by itself (Kerhervé 2015: about 34 bpm over the race), so don't speed up to reach the cap.
Method: the grade models set each segment's target.
safe: Descent: no power or HR target
gap.tip: GAP (grade-adjusted pace): Minetti's formula turns the pace on a slope into the equivalent flat pace. For reference only: it is off on steep climbs, descents and technical ground. A study pooling 674 data sets found Minetti's error largest uphill, and no grade formula has any data on technical terrain (Looney 2025); Koop also treats GAP as a direction only.
gap.note: The GAP column is Minetti's grade adjustment, for reference only: it is off on steep climbs, descents and technical ground (Looney 2025; Koop).
legend.gap_power: gap on the chart = power is only a reference here (steep, descent; grey in the table)
legend.gap_hr: gap on the chart = HR is only a reference on trail descents (grey in the table)
map.hint: hover the map or the profile to see the same point on both; switch basemaps top right
env.title: Conditions
env.tip: From = your usual training conditions (where your power was measured): the median altitude of your last 90 days of runs, temperature and humidity from the historical weather of those runs, else the median of all your activities. To = race day: with an event, date and place (peak, coordinates or the GPX start) the forecast is fetched on its own (CWA first: mountain forecast → township forecast; MET Norway only for dates or places CWA does not cover); a date more than 9 days ahead uses the mean of the same month (15 days either side of the race date) over the last 10 years, hour by hour. The difference becomes the environment factor M. Press ✎ to change them.
env.adv: Advanced: change From / To yourself (blue = changed by you; clear to go back to automatic)
env.to_wait: fetched once a date and place are set
env.need_date: fetched once the race date is set
env.need_loc: fetched once a place (peak, coordinates) or a GPX course is set
env.none: No automatic data; press ✎ to fill it in
env.clim_meta: , the same month over {years} {years|year|years}, mean of {models} models, temperature taken to this altitude
env.clim_partial: (some years missing; fetched again next time)
env.clim_hourly: ; includes each hour's mean (cool dawn, warm afternoon), so heat is set per segment
env.clim_night: The plan uses {t} °C, the mean over its {h} {h|hour|hours} on course: {n} of them outside 06–18 take the same hours' historical mean (daytime mean {day} °C, estimate)
env.cwa_summary: CWA authorization code (set by the site admin, shared by everyone)
env.cwa_shared: Set by the site admin, shared by everyone
env.cwa_note: Register free at opendata.cwa.gov.tw → Member → API authorization code. Only the site admin can set it (kept in the site folder's weather.json, or the CWA_API_KEY environment variable). Everyone's race weather starts with CWA; each forecast is downloaded once for the whole site and the cache is shared. Without a code, the MET Norway forecast is used (up to 9 days ahead).
env.route_sub: each segment uses its own section's forecast at the time you reach it (moved to its height); the rain, cold-wind, hypothermia and heat reminders are per section too
env.cairn: See this route's trip plan and live weather layers in Cairn ↗
env.town_meta: , township forecast: {name} ({km} km away), temperature moved from the township office's {from} m to {to} m ({dz} m, {dc} °C), humidity unchanged
rain.pop: highest chance of rain in the race window {p} %
dur.how: From your own-paced trail runs (group hikes left out): every 50 m, your grade curve is taken out, and within each activity the speed lost per extra hour after the first hour at the same grade and heart rate is measured (each activity has its own intercept, so the day's form and the trail surface cancel out); activities of ≥ 1.5 h are pooled into one slope, longer ones weighing more; it is then shrunk toward the 5%/h prior of Clark 2019 by precision (the prior counts as one measurement of ±2%/h, an estimate), and the prior is used when the leave-one-out error on runs of ≥ 1.5 h does not improve.
dur.none: No own-paced trail run of ≥ 1.5 h yet, so the 5%/h prior is used.
dur.measured: Your within-activity estimate: {v}% slower per hour{ci}, {n} {n|activity|activities};
dur.prior: the leave-one-out error was no better than the prior's, so the 5%/h prior is used.
how.title: How this was worked out
hint.carb_load: Carb-load the day before the race (how much, breakfast and caffeine: the carb-loading tile below)
hint.carb_load_2d: Carb-load 1–2 days before the race (how much, breakfast and caffeine: the carb-loading tile below)
hint.carb_normal: The day before the race, a normal high-carb day is enough (how much, breakfast and caffeine: the carb-loading tile below)
rain.card: Rain is possible during the race
poles.line: With poles: {what}; the first such segment is at {km} km
poles.up: steep climbs (≥ {g} %) feel easier at about the same speed
poles.down: steep descents (≤ −15 %) put 12–25 % less load on the knees
p30.tip: Follow the target power as a 30-second average, not the instant reading (it often spikes at the foot of a climb). Changing a number in the power column locks that segment; the others are redistributed and the average stays the same.
night.label: Night
night.tip: With a start time, the segments run between sunset and sunrise at the race location (from the weather forecast, else an astronomical formula) are marked Night and shaded dark on the chart. The night slowdown lengthens only the dark part of each segment; the ETAs and the finish move with it. At 0 % the prediction does not change at all. Not applied in target-time mode.
night.note: No study separates how much darkness alone slows you; Brager 2020's 35.9 % includes fatigue
heat.tip: Once the race-day weather is in and it has hourly data, each segment uses the temperature and dew point at the time you reach it, so a cool morning and a hot midday show in each segment's target. Hourly data come from the CWA 3-day forecast or the MET Norway forecast; a date more than 9 days ahead uses each hour's mean over the same month in the last 10 years. On a GPX course each segment's temperature is also moved to its own height (about 0.65 °C cooler per 100 m up, humidity unchanged). When the times change, the arrival times change too, and it recomputes until they settle. Without hourly data (CWA 1-week forecast, offline, weather not fetched yet) or without a start time, one temperature is used for the whole race.
heat.applied_clim: Applied: {n} {n|segment|segments} use the hourly mean of the same month over {years} {years|year|years}, {passes} passes
coros.title: Export to plan
coros.tip: Writes this race's legs as one session on race day in your training plan: edit each step on the Schedule page, then push it to the watch from there. On trails the watch's distance is often off (switchbacks, tree cover), so trail and hiking exports end every step with the lap button: press lap at the place the step names (aid station, top or bottom of a climb); the name also gives the predicted time and climb. On a road GPS is fine, so road exports use distance steps. Each step's target follows the segment targets: power ± 3 %; steep and walked climbs only an HR cap (no estimated power; open when there is no cap); none on trail descents. Hiking exports carry heart rate only (no power, no pace); a multi-day hiking trip cannot be exported, only a single-day one. The estimated training load counts legs without a target at the calculator's predicted race HR ÷ LTHR; after each race it is compared with the actual load for a personal correction (close to 1 with few races). One session per race: exporting again overwrites the last export.
coros.same: The plan already has this version
coros.restored: you deleted this session from the plan; it will be added back
coros.edited: This session was changed on the Schedule page: exporting overwrites your changes
coros.confirm_overwrite: This race session was changed on the Schedule page; exporting overwrites your changes. Overwrite?
coros.need_event: Pick the target race first: the export goes on that race's day
coros.push_hint: Once it is in the plan, push it to the watch from the Schedule page
coros.old_watch: The watch has this race from an earlier direct export: it is replaced the next time this session is pushed from the plan
coros.tss_hr: legs without a target at intensity {f} ({src})
coros.tss_default: no HR prediction: legs without a target at the default intensity {f}
coros.tss_nocalib: no post-race correction yet (compared with the actual load after each race)
coros.tss_kept: the Schedule keeps this number for the session (marked “race calculator estimate”); once its steps are changed on the Schedule page it is estimated from the structure
pick.title: Pick a location on the map
pick.hint: Click the map to drop a marker; drag it to fine-tune. Switch basemaps top right. A click within 300 m of a known peak also takes the peak's elevation.
goal.tip: Enter the goal as a pace (average pace or finish time) or as a power (average power in W or % CP): both are offered. The per-km / segment targets are spread from your goal by the grade model. No goal = the model's own prediction.
flat.s: Running this pace on the flat takes about the same effort as this race
flat.tip: Each segment's grade-adjusted pace (GAP, the segment table's GAP column) averaged by the segment's time: a climb counts as a faster flat pace, a descent at most 10 % slower. It is an effort, not a speed, and it leaves out altitude and technical ground. COROS Effort Pace is the same kind of conversion: runnable stretches (−3 to +15 %) pushed to COROS get an Effort Pace target. Garmin can't use it as a target: add a GAP (grade-adjusted pace) data field on the watch as a reference.
nm.tip_hike: Total time = each day's moving time + each day's stops (nights not included). Stops come from your earlier hike days, group and own-pace apart (the group / own-pace mark in the activity list; all hike days while few are marked), then by the route's highest point — low hills (< 1500 m), mid-altitude (1500–2999 m), Taiwan's 100 Peaks (Baiyue) country (≥ 3000 m), a past hike classed by its trip's highest point (with few trips in a class: ≥ 3000 / < 3000, then all hikes together) — predicted for each day's own moving time; the segment arrival times, night, cold and fuelling all use this timeline. {why}. The small text beside it is {range}. Minutes typed in the stop editor are added on top. Estimate.
nm.tip: Total time = moving time + stopped time. Stops are estimated by activity type (race / solo long run / hiking) from your earlier activities of the same type: the stopped share of the moving time grows with the moving time, stops growing after 2.5 hours, and is shrunk toward a prior when there are few activities; stops ≥ 60 s count as aid stations / queues, the rest as short pauses. {why}. The small figure beside it is {range}. Events marked as a trail race in the season plan use race stops, other trail plans use solo long run stops. There are no published aid-station numbers, so this is an estimate; typing minutes in the aid-station editor uses yours instead.
goal.vs_tip: Model = the Model prediction time (100 % effort) on the same course and weather. Faster by more than 3 % is flagged, by more than 8 % warned; the thresholds are an estimate.
goal.fast: {pct}% faster than the model: may not hold
goal.too_fast: {pct}% faster than the model: likely won't hold
zbar.axis_power: Palladino; axis = % CP, line = this race's average power, the coloured zone is the one the race is in
zbar.axis_hr: axis = heart rate in bpm, line = this race's predicted average heart rate, the coloured zone is the one the race is in
zbar.tip: This line is absolute intensity: which of your zones the race's average power or heart rate falls in — for reference only. What matters for a race is the effort bar above (relative intensity): how long you can hold this power, which depends on the race length — 85% CP is easy for 1 hour and hard for 8 hours. Power training shows power zones (Palladino's % CP), heart-rate training shows heart-rate zones (the training basis in Settings). “Zone details” lists every zone's name and range and lets you pick the heart-rate zone model; the default is the workout heart-rate zones in Settings.
zbar.line_power: Absolute intensity (reference): average {pct} CP ({w}), in Palladino zone {zone}
zbar.line_hr: Absolute intensity (reference): average {hr} bpm, in {sys} zone {zone}
zbar.no_hr_data: This calculation has no average heart rate, so the power zones are shown
surface.label: Trail surface
surface.meta: Flats and descents use your own dry / wet technicality factor (from {dry} stretches of 100 m marked dry and {wet} marked wet; estimate). No choice = as before, dry and wet data pooled
surface.meta_hr: The whole-race time still comes from the heart-rate model; the surface only changes how it is split: "wet" gives descents and flats more of the time (from {dry} stretches of 100 m marked dry and {wet} marked wet; estimate)
tdiff.label: Terrain difficulty
tdiff.tip: How hard the whole route's terrain is to move on. At the same grade and heart rate, harder ground is slower from the first hour on, whether or not you are tired.
tdiff.what_technical: lots of roots, loose rock and steep pitches; you often slow down to pick your footing
tdiff.what_scramble: sections that need ropes, climbing or your hands
tdiff.how: The multipliers are fitted from the trail runs you marked with a terrain difficulty in the activity list (each predicted from the others, then compared with the actual time); a level you have not marked uses an estimate. It scales the effort distance.
tdiff.no_hr: This plan's whole-race time does not come from the heart-rate pace model, so the terrain difficulty has no effect
strategy.tip: Even pace (road): the same average power all the way. Even effort (trail): the same effort all the way; on hills the power follows the hill flexibility below, so the pace changes with the grade rather than staying one pace. Negative / positive split: the power changes linearly from start to finish with the same race average. Most studies find the smallest spread between the halves fastest.
legend.hr_fade: Late in the race your HR drops by itself; don't speed up to reach the cap
fade: segment times follow your own pace change over the hours (estimate)
cad.title: Climbing cadence
cad.how: Counts only moving time with cadence on the 100 m stretches of 3 % or steeper, in your outdoor runs of the last year. Every walk / run split in the app is “cadence below 130 spm = walking”; on climbs cadence usually falls into a walking and a running group, and the line should sit in the valley between them. This only checks; it never moves the line.
rw.title: Walk–run transition speed
rw.default: Default values, none of your data yet: a grade needs at least 10 walked and 10 run windows.
rw.personal: Your transition speed is {d} m/s off the default ({n} windows, shrunk towards the default). The calculator's walk / run labels use it.
rw.how: Slower than the line, walking costs less; faster, running does. The default line comes from treadmill tests on high-level male runners (Brill & Kram 2021, Ortiz 2017); using it for everyone is an estimate. Your line: for every 2 % of grade, the speed at which half of your own 100 m windows are walked and half run; the median difference from the default, shrunk towards 0 by sample size and held within ±0.4 m/s (all estimates). Heart-rate crossovers are not used.
rw.legend_default: walk / run labels: default transition speed
rw.legend_you: walk / run labels: your transition speed
charts.neterr: No data: the connection dropped or the server did not answer (it may have just restarted or still be preparing the data).
ptrain.label: Enter it as training-conditions power (multiplied by the environment factor M)
ptrain.tip: Checked: the power you enter is what you hold in your usual training conditions; the calculator multiplies it by this race's environment factor M (altitude, temperature and humidity against your training; with segments, the distance-weighted mean of their M) to get the race-day power, then computes the finish time. E.g. 250 W at M 0.96 → 240 W on race day; %CP works the same. Unchecked: the number is the race-day power as it is.
formula.tip: Trail “Model prediction”: the finish time comes from the heart-rate pace model, which uses your own fitted climb divisor; this option only changes the comparison numbers, the RE details and the average power shown. “Target power”: the finish time is computed from this effort km, so changing it changes the finish time. “Target pace”: the finish time is your target; changing it changes the average power needed. Without a heart-rate model, “Model prediction” uses this formula too. With a GPX course and the segment model passed in the back-test, the finish time is the sum of the segment model and this formula has no effect.
sg.line: Walk or run by the predicted speed (SP-229, used in predictions only when the back-test improves): trail segment |error| {a} → {b}, climbs {c} → {d} ({n} {n|segment|segments}); the {k} {k|segment|segments} whose gait changed ({m} {m|activity|activities}) {e} → {f}. Needs at least {kmin} {kmin|segment|segments} over {mmin} {mmin|activity|activities}, and the changed segments more accurate.
sg.ok: better: predictions pick walk or run by the predicted speed
sg.no: worse: predictions keep the majority gait
sg.few: too few changed segments: predictions keep the majority gait
sg.tie: not better: predictions keep the majority gait
bt.th.title: Trail HR pace model back-test (race HR level, estimate)
bt.th.note: Positive = predicted slower than actual. The shape of the durability decay only shows in long races: compare whether the races ≥ {h} h have the smaller error with or without decay.
bt.th.none: No races of {h} h or longer: the decay shape for long races cannot be validated
bt.gf.title: Group hiking time back-test (group factor)
bt.gf.n: Your past group days: {n} {n|day|days} ({trips} {trips|trip|trips}), each trip predicted from the other trips only (leave one trip out).
bt.gf.used: The new one is more accurate: the group time in the calculator for Taiwan's 100 Peaks (Baiyue) uses the group factor
bt.gf.not_used: The new one is not more accurate: the group time in the calculator for Taiwan's 100 Peaks (Baiyue) keeps the group-day EP/h
bt.gf.none: Not enough hikes marked as group hikes (each trip needs other trips to compare with): no back-test.
bt.gf.alt: Altitude residual (what is left after the capacity model's altitude correction):
bt.gf.pack: Pack residual (what is left after the pack correction):
bt.gf.no_spread: can't be estimated (no spread over these days)
bt.gf.resid_note: The slope of the group days' actual ÷ capacity-model time against their mean altitude and pack weight ({n} {n|day|days}; standard error in brackets): near 0 means the correction is right, positive means that factor makes you slower than the model.
bt.gf.resid_few: Altitude and pack residuals: too few group days to estimate
bt.gf.solo: Days you hiked at your own pace: the capacity model's time error, median |error| {e}, bias {b} ({n} {n|day|days})
bt.gf.solo_none: Days you hiked at your own pace: none to compare
bt.sub: Back-tested on your past races and long activities: each one is estimated only from the data before that day, without that activity, then compared with what happened
snow.label: Snow
snow.tip: Snow time for winter mountains (rule of thumb, Japanese guides): climbs × 1.5 on a tracked trail, × 2–3 with no track. Only the climbs are multiplied; descents and flats stay the same
snow.note_trodden: Snow, tracked: climbing time × 1.5 (rule of thumb, Japanese guides), moving {t} ({base} without snow)
snow.note_untrodden: Snow, no track: climbing time × 2 to × 3 (rule of thumb, Japanese guides), moving {lo} (× 2) to {hi} (× 3), clock {clo} to {chi}; the numbers above use × 2
snow.season: Yushan main-peak trail snow-season rules (about mid-December to March, when Paiyun or Baimulin has ≥ 5 cm of snow): one-day ascents are suspended; crampons, an ice axe and a helmet are required, plus snow experience
sleep.changed: Sleep-point default changed: a new sleep point now gets minutes by the predicted race length (< 36 h 20 min, 36–60 h 30 min, > 60 h 90 min; Kishi 2024, Martin 2018). A blank sleep point here still counts 90 minutes, as before
sleep.changed_now: ; the new default for this race is {m} {m|minute|minutes}
noweight.banner: No body weight: the hiking walking-capacity model, the default pack, energy / fuelling and W/kg cannot be computed (trail / road predictions use your speed per watt instead). Enter it under Settings → Personal.
re.per_w_note: No body weight: RE is speed m/s ÷ power W (not per kg); the predictions use the same unit, so they still work. The road CVI adjustment becomes ±1 % per category (estimate). With a weight it goes back to per kg.
cp.test_mftp: CP test found on {date}: {label} → modelled threshold power {cp}. The plan's CP uses the same fit by itself (it changes only by 3 W or more); nothing to set.
split.mismatch: {k} day ends, but {n} {n|day|days} need {m}: each day gets the same distance for now (estimate). Add or remove day ends, or change the days, in "Day split preview"
split.osm_note: 🛖 = the built-in list of Taiwan's huts (within 150 m of the route), data from
split.equal: No day ends yet: each of the {n} {n|day|days} gets the same distance for now (estimate), and the summit day may be wrong. Open "Day split preview" and tap a candidate or the profile where each day ends
overnight.how: A stop of ≥ {h} h or the watch off all night counts as a night (estimate). See each day's distance, climb and time in the preview first; nothing changes until you press OK.
overnight.event_days: This trip is {d} {d|day|days} in the season plan: the calculator will use {n}; change the days in the season plan to match
ground.label: Ground
ground.loading: Looking up the ground in the trail dictionary (OpenStreetMap)…
ground.unknown_ok: The calculation does not need it.
ground.tip: Every stretch is sorted by the ways within 60 m of the course in the trail dictionary (rebuilt monthly from OpenStreetMap). Dirt trail: earth, roots, rock and other unstable ground (OSM surface ground / dirt / rock …, or sac_scale ≥ mountain_hiking, or a very bad smoothness), and a path without a surface tag out of town (mountain paths are nearly all dirt). Man-made: asphalt, concrete, laid stones, boardwalks, stone steps, gravel forest roads, roads. Unsure: a path without a surface tag in town (it may be a paved park path, so nothing is guessed), or no way within 50 m. The unsure stretches are dashed on the map: click one to mark it dirt or man-made, or type the split yourself. Kept with this course: the same GPX brings it back.
ground.sum: The three must add up to 100 %
ground.map_unsure: Dashed: ground unsure — click to mark it dirt or man-made
ground.tech: Trail technicality on the dirt only: {applied} % of the flats and descents (incl. {unsure} % unsure, kept as dirt); the {made} % man-made goes without
ground.tech_tip: The trail technicality (how much slower than predicted you run trail flats and descents) used to apply to the whole course. With TRC_TECH_DIRT_ONLY it applies to the dirt only: the man-made stretches (asphalt, concrete, stone steps, forest roads) use your plain running RE; the unsure ones keep it. Only segments ≤ +2 %.
split.cands_n: Day-end candidates: {list} (choose them in "Day split preview")
cairn.sched_line: The group's walking time {t} ({clock} with the stops)
cairn.sched_rest: minus the {m} min of stops written in the timetable
cairn.sched_ratio: no stops written: × the group moving ratio {pct} %, {src}
cairn.ratio_yours: the median of your {n} past group hikes
cairn.sched_go: ⏱ Use the group's time as the target
cairn.sched_partial: The group's timetable only goes to {km} km ({pct} % of the route), so it can't give a target time for the whole trip.
group.title: Following the group
group.sub: the group's timetable vs your capacity, leg by leg
group.tip: Your time is the calculator's capacity time (your walking at AeT, with grade, pack, altitude and the hours into the day), whatever the target-time mode or heart-rate band. Effort = the metabolic rate the group's speed needs ÷ your rate at AeT (the capacity model run the other way: Pandolf forwards); downhill it compares speeds. The cut points are estimates: < 80 % waiting, 80–95 % easy, 95–105 % right (about AeT), 105 % to your ceiling hard, above the ceiling or 10 % slower than the group can't keep up. No heart-rate numbers: your steep-grade speed barely changes with the heart-rate band, so only zones are given. Multi-day fatigue is not counted. The timetable is read only and never written back to Cairn; the calculator's own estimate does not change.
group.head: The group's pace is mostly "{tier}" for you;
group.head_behind: Legs where you may fall behind ({n}): {list}.
group.head_nobehind: no leg where you fall behind.
group.head_hard: Legs above AeT add up to {h}.
group.rest_ratio: On days without stops in the timetable the group's moving time = the time between rows × the group moving ratio {pct} % (estimate). Stops counted as walking would make the group look slower and the effort look lower.
group.rest_cairn: The group's moving time = the time between rows minus the stops written in the timetable.
group.speed_only: No walking-capacity model yet (it needs running data): speeds only, your time ÷ the group's.
group.pack: On a guided trip porters often carry the shared food and the guide does the meals; a pack set too heavy overstates the effort — change each day's pack above.
group.close: National parks have cut-off times (e.g. Yushan main peak: turn back if not at Paiyun Lodge by 10:00); check them against the timetable — they are not computed here.
group.long_hard: over 3 h above AeT: hard to hold
group.cut.behind: above the ceiling or 10 % slower than the group
group.zone.wait: below AeT: the group is much slower — heart rate held low, often waiting (such days don't feed your capacity calibration)
group.zone.easy: below AeT: room to spare, you can chat
group.zone.right: about AeT: the ideal intensity for a multi-day trip
group.zone.hard: between AeT and threshold: not sustainable for more than about 3 h in a row
group.zone.behind: near threshold or above: a very high intensity, or you fall behind
group.zone_down.wait: downhill: the group is much slower, you'll wait
group.zone_down.easy: downhill: slower than your usual, easier on the legs
group.zone_down.hard: downhill: faster than your usual — it costs the legs, not the lungs
group.zone_down.behind: downhill: much faster than your descent speed — you fall behind, and it is hardest on the legs
ds.label: Start time each day (day 1 = the start time above; empty = same as day 1; a group timetable fills them in)
dl.tip: Multi-day fatigue and the next day's recovery have no model good enough (the multi-day factor is 1.0), so here are numbers you can compare: the day's EP (km + climb/100) against your hardest day on foot (highest EP), and the metres down with the pack (descending with a pack is what makes the next day's legs sore). After a day with ≥ 1,000 m down with the pack, or over 3 h above AeT following a group, the next day says to go slower for the first hour (the thresholds are estimates).
dl.rec_tip: A big descent with the pack (or a long time above AeT) the day before: go slower for the first hour (estimate)
dl.ref: Your hardest day on foot = your hiking day with the highest EP: {date}, EP {ep} ({km} km, {gain} m climb)
dl.noref: No hiking day recorded yet to compare with (hiking or mountaineering activities)
cairn.sched_mixed: minus the {m} min of stops written; days without stops × the group moving ratio {pct} %, {src}
share.cairn_curve: Attach the time curve for Cairn

stop.tip: One aid station per row, sorted by km. The type sets the fuelling plan: a water station gives water only; an aid station has food and water, and the carbs due near it are eaten at the station; a major aid station adds electrolytes and hot food; a medical station has no supplies (carry enough water from the previous one); a self-supported refuel point is your own drop bag. A blank stop time uses the default (water station 0.5, aid station 2, major aid station 5, self-supported 2 min; estimates) and is added to the ETA. When the GPX waypoints are named like aid stations (CP1, Aid, water…) you can Import from course. A non-stop race (its format in the season plan) has one more type, the sleep point: enter its km and how long you sleep (minutes); the sleep counts in the ETA. A new sleep point gets a default from the predicted total time: < 36 h 20 min each, 36–60 h 30 min (about 1–1.5 h in total in studies), > 60 h 90 min (sleeping every night, about 8 h in total; Martin 2018); most runners nap between 00:00 and 05:00, and 82 % of the naps are under 30 min (Kishi 2024). The brackets are estimates; a blank time still counts as 90; the race assessment compares the hardest stretch between two sleep points.

hills.tip: On climbs the power may go a little above the average and on descents it is let drop naturally; the average power stays the same. Up to +5% on climbs has no extra physiological cost; the limit is 12%. A climb that would stay above CP too long is scaled back automatically.

hrband.label: HR band
hrband.tip: Guided group: the main number is the time your past group days' EP/h give, with your capacity time beside it; on your own: the main number is your capacity time. Capacity time = your walking capacity at AeT (the steep walking windows of your trail runs plus the climbing windows of your hikes at HR ≥ AeT, shaped by the Pandolf physiological prior). HR band: once the heart-rate lag is handled, the speed on steep climbs still does not change with heart rate, so there are only two settings, AeT and Ceiling. A blank pack uses the default pack: 4 kg for one day, 9 kg for several (estimates); after 3 trips with a recorded pack your own median is used, or set it in Settings → Advanced settings; on multi-day trips −0.7 kg each day after the first (food, estimate); a GPX with no day ends is split evenly by the days. Each segment's temperature comes from the race-day temperature (at the Altitude of the temperature) with a lapse rate of 0.0065 K/m.

rg.title: Riegel analysis
rg.sub: ln power vs ln time; slope = k
rg.tip:
What Riegel is: the longer you go, the less power you can hold. Your best powers of the past year (the highest for each duration) are drawn as a line and fitted with a straight line (ln power vs ln time); its slope is k.
How to read it: the more negative k is (e.g. −0.10), the faster power falls with time, so a long race needs a much lower power than a short effort; the closer k is to 0, the better your endurance.
Chart: the blue line is your best-power envelope, the orange line your own fit, the dashed line the k looked up from CP and TTE, and the dot this prediction. A big gap between your line and the lookup line usually means too few long all-out records.
How far to trust it: look at R² (the closer to 1, the better the fit), the number of points, and whether it is marked usable. With fewer than 3 long all-out efforts there is no fit and it shows not enough data.
How to use it: usually leave it alone. When your own fit is unreliable, set Riegel k to lookup in Advanced settings.

oc.th_tip: The all-out heart rate falls with race duration: x*(T) = x₀ − s·ln(T). The shape prior comes from the literature (Fornasiero 2018: 77% HRmax on average over a 65 km all-out race; Kerhervé 2015: heart rate falling as the race goes on over 106 km), anchored at 1.00 for 0.5 h, 0.90 for 3 h and 0.85 for 12 h × LTHR; {fit}, shrunk towards the prior when there are few samples. Durability decay {d}% per hour; the speed at the same heart rate levels off once it is down to {vf}%: {dur} Heat: your β of 0.224 bpm per Hadley unit moves the heart-rate level to the race day's heat, with no separate Hadley time penalty on top.

fuel.tip: Energy comes from the predicted segment power and times; carbs, water and sodium are ranges by race type, predicted time and each segment's temperature. The ? beside each number has the method and sources. There is no personal sweat rate or gut-training record, so the water is a general range and the carbs stay at or under 90 g/h.
fuel.k_tip_hike: Moving energy = the Pandolf equation (weight, the day's pack, each segment's speed and grade) summed over the segments; Pandolf doesn't apply downhill, so descents are estimated with Minetti's walking curve. The range includes Yamamoto (the app's original hiking energy): Pandolf often underestimates heavy packs.
fuel.k_tip: Power method: each segment's running power × time ÷ (22.1 % × 4.184), with 21.6 % on grades > 4 %. Grades > 8 %, walked segments and descents use 1.07 kcal/kg/km × Minetti's grade ratio instead. The power meter's own “kJ ≈ kcal” undercounts by about 8 %: for running, kJ can't be taken as kcal. Range ±10–15 %: individual differences, fatigue and the underestimate on steep climbs together.
fuel.c_tip_hike: Low intensity over several days: the low end of the ultra advice, a snack every 45–60 min, 30–50 g each. What matters is each day's total energy.
fuel.c_tip_short: Under 75 min: a mouth rinse or a few carbs is enough.
fuel.c_tip_half: Up to 2–2.5 h: 30–60 g per hour.
fuel.c_tip_ultra: Over 6 h: start at 30–50 g/h and work up towards 60–90 g/h if your gut takes it. Use glucose + fructose.
fuel.c_tip: 2–6 h: 60–90 g per hour, as glucose + fructose (e.g. 2:1 gels) so it can be absorbed. There is no gut-training record, so no more than 90 g/h; start at 60 and practise on long runs.
fuel.w_tip_hike: Drink Yamamoto's amount (70–80 % of the moving energy, in ml); don't force fluids; check your urine colour and weight every day.
fuel.thirst_s: cool day, short race · don't drink so much you gain weight
fuel.thirst_tip: In a short race on a cool day, drinking when thirsty is enough; drinking too much brings a risk of low blood sodium.
fuel.no_gain: · don't drink so much you gain weight
fuel.w_tip: Moves within 400–800 ml/h with each segment's temperature: cool segments near the low end, hot ones (the hottest quarter or ≥ 25 °C) near the top. The ceiling is your own sweat rate; your weight must not go up during the race. Sweat is not worked back from energy (1 L of sweat ≈ 580 kcal is heat given off, not energy burned).
fuel.na_tip_hike: Electrolyte tablets, about 200–300 mg per hour; soup and sauces at dinner count too.
fuel.na_tip: 300–600 mg per hour, towards the top on hot segments. Sodium slows the fall in blood sodium but can't prevent the low blood sodium that drinking too much causes.
fuel.rest_tip: Rest time = 24 h − moving time, at the Mifflin-St Jeor resting metabolism × a camp activity factor of 1.3 (estimate). Height {h} cm ({hs}), age {age} ({ag}), {sex} ({ss}).
fuel.food_tip: Food per day = the daily total (the higher of Pandolf / Yamamoto) × 85 % replaced ÷ 4.4 kcal/g. 4.4 kcal/g is the thru-hikers' rule of 125 kcal per ounce; a deficit of about 500 kcal a day is fine for 3–5 days. On a guided trip the guide usually handles dinner, so you carry a bit less.
fuel.bfast: Breakfast: {g}, 1–4 h before the start (1–4 g/kg). {drink}. Caffeine (optional): {caf}, 30–90 min before the start.
fuel.dehyd_tip: No personal sweat-rate record: at race pace about 1.0 L/h on a cool day and 1.75 L/h at 30 °C, scaled by each segment's hourly burn ÷ 700 kcal (walk slowly and you sweat less; estimate), minus the water drunk as suggested; the suggested water never goes above this sweat rate. Beyond 2 % of body weight performance drops, but don't drink so much that your weight goes up just to make it all up.
fuel.dehyd_src: ACSM 2007 (Sawka): dehydration no more than 2 % of body weight; Baker 2017: sweat rates 0.5–2.0 L/h
fuel.deficit: Gap about {k} kcal (covered by your glycogen)
fuel.sched_tip_hike: Counted from each day's start: a snack every 45–60 min, on the climbs where you can (easier to eat while walking).
fuel.sched_tip: Every 20–30 min (solids are fine in the first half, gels or drinks in the second); eaten at the aid station when one is near; on walked or steep uphill stretches where you can, never on steep descents. Water to carry between aid stations = water per hour × time × 1.2 (20 % extra).
